messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - canary-deploy-errors on inference-api (multiple 5xx)

incident-bot: Alert rule: deploy.canary.5xx_rate > 3% for 2m

sara: oncall here, seeing spikes on /v1/generate across eu-west-1 canary pods. Going to look at the deploy canary.

jamal: i can see a new image pushed ~10m ago: registry.redwood.internal/ml/inference-api:canary-20260315. CI job id 4827. Pulling logs.

marco: quick note — CI changed the tagging step to repoint latest-canary -> immutable-sha, but looks like the pipeline used an older base image. possible retag / cache shadowing at registry.

kai: can someone paste the deploy event? i want to see which replicaSet is active.

jamal: kubectl -n prod get rs -l app=inference-api -o wide
```
NAME                         DESIRED   CURRENT   READY   AGE
inference-api-5d4b7c9f       3         3         3       1h
inference-api-6a7f8b2a-canary 1         1         0       12m
```

jamal: canary pod is CrashLoopBackOff with 5xx responses in logs. grabbing pod logs now.

jamal: ```
2026-03-15T12:03:21Z ERROR handler.go:87 request_id=abc123 upstream=bad-image init: invalid model checksum
2026-03-15T12:03:22Z WARN cache.go:214 model layer mismatch for model:v2 expecting checksum=sha256:aaa got sha256:bbb
```

anya: that looks like a layer mismatch + runtime fail when loading weights. sounds like artifact retagged to the same tag but different content (mutable tag). classic cache poisoning/registry shadowing.

sara: ok hypothesis: CI published artifact A -> retagged later to artifact B under same tag, canary pulled B (incompatible) due to registry propagation, causing runtime 5xx. impact limited to canary but traffic routed by global load balancer -> some percentage saw errors.

kai: what's current error rate? dashboards?

marco: Cloud metrics: region eu-west-1 all instances 5xx rate jumped to 4.2% in last 3m. Canary-only subset is ~1% of traffic but GCLB sticky routing sent some cross-zone. Customer-facing error increase reported by monitoring.

sara: immediate mitigation: 1) flip feature flag canary-rollout.enabled=false (kill-switch) 2) pause CI triggers 3) rollback canary to previous immutable rs or scale down canary pods. I'll flip flag and then rollback.

jamal: acknowledged. applying flag now -> toggling via flags-console API.

jamal: PATCH /flags/canary-rollout {"enabled": false} -> 200 OK

marco: pause pipeline: disabling downstream promotion job 4827 in Jenkins.

sara: rolling back canary now: kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/inference-api --to-revision=2

kai: copying command to exec on cluster: kubectl -n prod scale deployment/inference-api-6a7f8b2a-canary --replicas=0 && kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/inference-api

jamal: canary pods terminated, rollout status shows stable replicaSet 5d4b7c9f active.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident acknowledged by on-call (sara). Priority: P1 - customer visible errors.

marco: after rollback 5xx rate dropped to 0.6% in 2m. dashboards back to baseline.

anya: will need a postmortem on registry tagging safeguards: enforce immutable tags, registry lifecycle audit and CI policy to prevent retagging. Also add a job that verifies image digest in deployment vs CI artifact manifest.

kai: customers impacted: small set of prod API keys 12 customers saw elevated errors. cs-notify suggested a brief message: "We experienced intermittent API errors during a canary deployment; rollout paused and service restored. No data loss."

sara: sending handoff to jamal for post-incident followup and RCA. jamal you're next oncall for the drift window.

jamal: taking handoff. i'll collect CI logs, registry audit, and correlate push events -> set followup action items.

marco: TODOs: (1) block mutable retags in registry (2) CI gate: manifest digest pin check (3) add early-canary digest verification script (4) run a canary-only traffic isolation test during rollout.

sara: thanks everyone. reopening as postmortem thread later. closing incident channel now. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident P1 CLOSED by sara at 2026-03-15T12:20:00Z
